Subject: AuroraPay integration — auth options, SDK setup, and short POC next steps

Hi Alex — thanks again for the demo earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single place to track action items: 

Summary from call:
- Goal: 2-week POC to validate reconciliation pipeline using Redwood embeddings + reranker for transaction matching, and a structured output tool-call to return normalized ledger entries.
- High-level integration: AuroraPay will run POC in a sandbox (us-west) and call Redwood’s hosted API. We discussed two auth flows: short-lived API tokens via a token-exchange (recommended) or long-lived API keys for initial testing.

Open technical items / asks:
1) Auth: do you prefer service-account JWTs (recommended by your procurement) or temporary API keys for the initial run?
2) SDK: we’ll provide a small SDK quickstart and a Docker example for local testing.
3) Routing/latency: POC will point to us-west; if you need multi-region we can configure routing by region/model.
4) Structured output: we’ll ship a sample tool-calling schema for ledger normalization (JSON schema included in the SDK PDF).
5) Embeddings & rerankers: propose using Redwood’s embeddings for candidate retrieval + a small reranker model for precision — will include evaluation prompt-set for you to run.

Proposed next steps (priority):
- You confirm preferred auth approach (service account JWT vs temp key) — Alex
- Redwood sends SDK quickstart + JWT snippet — Monica (attached: redwood-sdk-setup.pdf, aurorapay-poc-checklist.xlsx)
- Schedule 45m infra demo week of Mar 26 to validate token exchange and network egress — Ben

If you’re ok, I can provision a temporary API key scoped to sandbox for you to exercise the flow while Monica prepares the JWT example.

Thanks — looking forward.

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0112

Date: Thu, 22 Mar 2028 12:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: AuroraPay integration — auth options, SDK setup, and short POC next steps

Alex — looping in a short technical note with options and a sample snippet (attached jwt-svc-account-snippet.txt). Long story short:

Options we recommend:
A) Service-account JWT + short-lived tokens (recommended for production)
   - Aurora creates a service account identity in your IdP or KMS and we exchange a signed JWT via Redwood’s token-exchange endpoint to get a scoped bearer token.
   - TTLs: Redwood issues tokens with configurable TTLs down to 5 minutes; typical POC TTL = 1 hour. Refresh flows supported via the SDK.

B) Scoped temporary API keys (fine for quick POC)
   - Keys can be restricted by route/model and IP egress. Rotation for API keys is manual or via API.

Implementation notes / sample flow:
- Step 1: We’ll create a Redwood service-account for AuroraPay (unique suffix) and pre-configure allowed scopes (generate_embeddings, model_infer, tool_call).
- Step 2 (token exchange): Aurora signs a JWT (RS256) with your key and calls POST /token-exchange -> returns short-lived bearer token.
- SDK: our Node/Python SDKs support automatic token refresh and will accept either API key or bearer token. Example curl is in the attached snippet.

Networking: if you require egress via a specific IP range we can add allowlist entries for the POC environment.

I’ve attached a tiny snippet and will push a quick example repo this afternoon to the shared drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/0AexampleSharedDriveLink

Monica Patel
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.com

Attachments: jwt-svc-account-snippet.txt (example token-exchange curl + SDK snippet)
